title: An inspector table
description:
Describe a struct's fields once and use the description to show and edit them as text.

```
name    = "Goblin"
health  = 30
speed   = 2.5
hostile = true
set speed "3" -> 3
set health "lots" -> refused: not a whole number
```
hints: A lambda per field: `{"health", [](const Monster& m) { return std::to_string(m.health); }, [](Monster& m, const std::string& s) { ... }}` (lesson 5.03).
requirements: A field description holds a name and functions to read the value as text and to set it from text.
Build the table for a `Monster` struct with a `std::vector` of descriptions.
Setting checks the text and refuses bad values with a message.
stretch: Make a template `field("speed", &Monster::speed)` that builds the lambdas from a member pointer. Member pointers are not covered in this course: look up "pointers to data members" (`T Monster::*`) first.
